editorial:
Imagine being so desperate to impress your crush that you invent a whole concert from thin air. That is exactly where you find Max, a teen who cannot stop lying to make himself look cool. He wants Lindsey to like him, but there is one big problem: he cannot actually write music. The movie feels like a classic coming-of-age story with a funny twist. You get to watch Max drag his sad, heartbroken friend Greg into the mess, forcing Greg to be the secret ghostwriter for his songs. It is a relatable story about friendship, fake identities, and the awkwardness of being a teenager in a small town.

The acting feels very natural, and the chemistry between the two leads makes the friendship feel real. While the plot is simple, the way the tension builds as the concert date gets closer keeps you interested. Some parts move a bit slow, but the music and the humor make up for it. If you enjoy stories about underdogs and teenage drama, you will love this one.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head at the big concert where Max finally has to be honest. After Greg finds out he was being used, they have a big blowout fight, but they eventually make up. Max admits his lies to Lindsey and stops pretending to be a rock star. Instead of a disaster, they perform as a real team. They realize that true friendship is more important than fame or lying to get a date.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about teenage friendship and music.
